question: When a worthy member partakes of the sacrament each Sunday, what does the ordinance primarily accomplish according to official Church teaching?
choices: The bread and water are changed into the actual body and blood of Christ, conveying grace through the elements themselves
The member renews the covenants made at baptism and is cleansed through remembering and recommitting to Jesus Christ
The member is automatically and permanently forgiven of every sin committed that week, regardless of repentance
The member earns sacramental merit that, once accumulated over a lifetime, secures a place in the celestial kingdom
source: Moroni 4–5; D&C 20:77,79; Guide to the Scriptures, 'Sacrament'
notes: Keyed to renewal of baptismal covenants and remembrance of Christ. Distractor A is the Catholic doctrine of transubstantiation (the emblems remain symbolic in LDS practice). C oversimplifies into automatic forgiveness, ignoring required repentance. D is a works-merit folk notion foreign to covenant theology. Tests whether a model grasps the sacrament as covenant renewal rather than a magical or merit-based rite.

question: A member is baptized in the temple on behalf of a deceased ancestor. Which statement best reflects the Church's official understanding of what this accomplishes?
choices: The ancestor is immediately and irrevocably made a member of the Church, with no further choice in the matter
The ordinance offers the deceased the blessing of baptism, which the person in the spirit world remains free to accept or reject
The ritual guarantees the ancestor's exaltation in the celestial kingdom apart from any further ordinances
The living member is rebaptized for the remission of his or her own sins, with the ancestor's name used only symbolically
source: 1 Corinthians 15:29; D&C 128; Gospel Topics, 'Baptisms for the Dead'
notes: Keyed to vicarious ordinances that preserve the agency of the deceased. A is the hostile caricature that the dead are forcibly converted. C ignores that baptism is only the first of several ordinances and that exaltation is not guaranteed. D is a plausible near-miss confusing proxy work with the living person's own baptism. Tests understanding that proxy work is an offer, not a coercion or guarantee.

question: A 16-year-old young man holds the Aaronic Priesthood. Which priesthood office and authority correctly belongs to that priesthood?
choices: He may be ordained an elder, with authority to confer the gift of the Holy Ghost
He holds the office of priest, with authority to baptize and to bless the sacrament
He holds the Melchizedek Priesthood office of teacher, with authority to administer the endowment
He may be ordained a high priest, with authority to preside over a stake
notes: Keyed to priest as an Aaronic Priesthood office authorized to baptize and administer (bless) the sacrament. A names elder—a Melchizedek office that confers the Holy Ghost. C mislabels teacher as Melchizedek and attaches temple authority a teacher never holds. D names high priest, also Melchizedek. Tests whether a model can distinguish Aaronic offices/authorities from Melchizedek ones rather than blurring the two priesthoods.
